title: Fugitive considered threat to officers
subtitle: RCMP killed sniper in motel standoff
article: In the last moments of his life, Danny Sand, 21, took a position high on a motel roof, crouched low and levelled his high-powered rifle at the RCMP tactical unit that surrounded him.

Along with his brother Robert and Robert's lover, Laurie Bell, Danny was wanted that snowy, windy day, Dec. 21, 2001, for the murder of RCMP Const. Dennis Strongquill, 52. The officer had been shot to death 14 hours earlier in Russell, Man.

Strongquill and his partner were shot at after pulling over a truck whose driver failed to lower its high beams. They raced to the detachment at Russell where the truck rammed their cruiser. Strongquill was shot dead and the suspects fled.
Twenty police officers surrounded the motel in Wolseley, Sask., where the Sand brothers and Bell had been hiding out.
RCMP sniper Al Lukasewich hid behind haystacks in a field about 100 metres from the motel. The sniper sighted fugitive Danny Sand through his scope.
"We have a shot," Lukasewich's partner Const. Bob Gourlay reported to the RCMP command centre. "Sierra-team has a shot. We're gonna take him out."
"Go ahead," replied Staff Sgt. Bob Bazin from the police command centre.
Lukasewich pulled the trigger and the bullet hit Sand in the head, killing him.

In a Brandon court Tuesday, the Crown went over a tape of radio communications of the RCMP's siege, and also called a number of police witnesses, who detailed how the RCMP shot Danny Sand, then arrested Robert, 24, and Laurie Bell, 21.

Sand and Bell are on trial for first-degree murder. The Crown alleges that after shooting Strongquill, the three fugitives fled through the night, stealing vehicles and shooting at pursuers until they lost the police. The threesome took refuge at the small motel in Wolseley, population 800, along the Trans-Canada Highway, 90 kilometres east of Regina.
In the early afternoon, police snipers took up positions around the motel.
When Danny Sand climbed up on the motel roof and took up his firing position, RCMP team leader Cpl. Dave Horn believed he was a threat to officers stationed across the highway.
"He had the advantage of having a higher observation point, in essence, a sniper position," Horn testified.
A minute after Lukasewich shot Danny Sand, Laurie Bell, then Robert Sand gave up.
